scope: Keep every retained ground damage-over-time effect, including expansion and buff-table content, under classic potency, dissipation, and absorption authority without allowing inherited NGE expertise, vulnerability, armor, generic damage, repeat pulse-resistance, universal/group DOT immunity, or full-damage-immunity layers to modify players.

findings: Publish 14.1 applies authored DOT strength after an application resistance check, reduces duration through the matching dissipation skill modifier, and reduces each pulse through the matching classic absorption modifier capped at 50 percent.

The pinned Publish 14.1 implementation has no NGE DOT-increase expertise, DOT vulnerability, all-DOT expertise absorption, armor-derived DOT mitigation, generic multiply/divide-damage modifiers, or second resistance roll on every pulse.

The inherited shared DOT library contained all of those later layers and was reachable from authenticated PRE-CU combat actions, restored Combat Medic poison/disease medicine, retained expansion actions, and buff-table pulse handlers.

The inherited buff framework also admitted later dot_resist_* and damage_immune modifiers, universal player DOT purges, and a second application-immunity consumer family absent from the pinned Publish 14.1 implementation.

Retained quests, expansion zones, and compatibility callers keep their authored DOT type, strength, duration, effects, and messaging, but now resolve through the same Publish 14.1 application and pulse rules as original content.
